newsitem.title: CANADA: 10-year sunspot forecast - calm and milder.
newsitem.headline: 10-year sunspot forecast - calm and milder.

text.p: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration and other researchers on Tuesday gave an optimistic 10-year weather forecast for the Sun, which could mean cooler temperatures and less electronic tumult on Earth.

Scientists from NASA and the astronomy department at Yale University predicted a decrease in sunspots on the solar surface, as well as a decrease in magnetic storms, cosmic rays and ionosphere disturbances.

Such a mild forecast, which the researchers acknowledged was at variance with many other predictions, could signal cooler weather on Earth, fewer power blackouts and less interference with radio waves.
The sun's magnetic activity tends to run on an approximate 10-year cycle, the scientists said in a statement.
If the current cycle that started in September 1996 follows the NASA-Yale prediction, it would reverse a 400-year-old trend toward greater solar activity.
It could also help moderate global warming and ease the efforts of NASA and others whose high-technology equipment is sometimes affected by solar storms, the researchers said.

In addition, they said the decrease in solar cosmic rays would cut down on "glitches" in sophisticated electronic systems of satellites. It might even cut the risk of widespread power blackouts caused in the past by large solar storms.
The scientists admitted that the sun's magnetic activity, which churns its hot gases and spawns the eruption of so-called sunspots, was highly unpredictable.
They made their forecast using solar telescopes which gathered data on the Sun's magnetic fields. They presented their findings at a meeting of the American Astronomical Society in Toronto.
